title: Hang an electric fence wire on insulators only
instruction: This electric fence wire will be switched on later. Hang it in the white insulator slots on all three posts so that no part of the wire or its yellow handle touches a post or the table: keep it at least 1 cm from every post and let the handle hang free past the last post. Then let go of the wire.
context: Electric fence guides: "Insulators are used to prevent the conductor or wire touching the posts or stakes, which could lead to power leakage" (AHDB); "Both wooden and metal posts require post insulators to prevent the wires from touching the posts" (NJDEP Fish & Wildlife). O*NET 45-2093.00 farmworkers: "Inspect, maintain, and repair equipment, machinery, buildings, pens, yards, and fences". The whole wire must stay off grounded posts, not just reach the supports.
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Four grey 25 x 25 mm square posts, 18 cm tall, fixed, centres at x 30: corner post y +31, line posts y +15, 0, -15. Each line post has a white offset insulator: a 19 mm standoff arm (12 wide, 8 thick) off the post's robot side holding an open-top U slot running along y (20 mm long, 14 mm inner gap, 4 mm walls 10 mm above an 8 mm floor), slot centre at x 25.75, floor top 15 cm above the table. Corner post: white strain-insulator block 40 x 20 x 20 mm on its front face, centred 15.3 cm high. Wire: white 6 mm polyrope, 53.5 cm, tied off 6 mm past the block's -y face (x 25.75, y 29.4), with a yellow gate handle (40 x 14 x 12 mm, 10 g) on its free end. Start: the wire hangs from the block to the table and lies roughly straight in front of the posts, handle flat at about x 15, y -20 (see screenshot).
scoring: Score 0 if: either gripper is within 3 cm of the wire or handle; the wire does not lie inside all three insulator slots (between the walls, below the wall tops); any part of the wire or handle touches a post (gap under 3 mm, feeler gauge); any part of the wire or handle is less than 2 cm above the table; a post or insulator was moved. Otherwise 1.0 if every part of the wire and handle is at least 1 cm from every post body (ruler), 0.5 if the smallest gap is 3-10 mm. Touching insulators is allowed. Success (1.0) when this holds for 1 s with the wire at rest.
reset_notes: Lift the wire out of the slots, let it hang from the corner block and lay the rest straight on the table towards the tape mark at x 15, y -20 where the handle lies flat. Check that all posts and insulators are at their marks.
fidelity: Wire: 27 rigid segments of about 2 cm (octagonal colliders) with bending springs, no twist or stretch, standing in for polyrope; the corner tie-off is a weld; the handle is a rigid box welded to the end. The wire spawns straight at wire height and falls. Posts and insulators are fixed rigid boxes (PLA in a real build), no current: touching is judged geometrically (wire centre line minus radius, handle axis minus half-diagonal). Real trials use an unpowered wire and a feeler gauge.
